tech_stack: .NET 6/C#, SQL Server (Dapper), Azure Blob Storage, Kafka (Confluent Avro), Azure Cache for Redis

http_deps: CMS3 — legacy content store via SOAP/REST hybrid
UMS — user lookup and identity resolution
background_services: ScheduleActivateBackgroundService — activates scheduled content at trigger time
ExpirationBackgroundService — scans and flags expired content
CustomPropertyBackgroundService — processes custom property merge jobs
ContentEventConsumer — Kafka consumer for content-event topic
VFSEventListener — Kafka consumer for video processed events
CrackingPipelineMetaEventListener — Kafka consumer for CCP metadata
CustomPropertyEventListener — Kafka consumer for custom property changes
ExpirationNotificationSettingListener — Kafka consumer for expiration settings
AugmentationEventListener — Kafka consumer for static augmentation events

domains.name: File
domains.responsibility: Manages the lifecycle of content files including creation, checkout/checkin, versioning, variants, and file-level metadata.
domains.health_reason: FileModel and ItemModel are pure data bags with 30+ public get/set properties and no invariant-enforcing methods; checkout state, expiry, and version status are mutated externally in FileWriter static methods rather than inside the entity.

invariants: A file cannot be checked out by a second user while already checked out
A file cannot be published unless it has at least one active version
A file cannot be deleted while checked out
Batch checkout cannot exceed CMConstant.LIMIT_BATCHSIZE_CHECKOUT items

domains.name: Folder
domains.responsibility: Manages folder hierarchy, folder navigation, folder creation/deletion/move, and folder-level access checks.
domains.health_reason: Folder objects are plain data structures passed through FolderOrchestrator; business rules (e.g. cannot delete non-empty folder) are enforced in FolderWriter rather than in a folder entity.

invariants: A folder cannot be deleted if it contains child items
A folder cannot be moved into one of its own descendants
Root folder cannot be renamed or deleted

domains.name: Item
domains.responsibility: Provides the unified content item model that represents any content object (file, folder, shortcut) and manages relationships, shortcuts, and URL mappings.
domains.health_reason: ItemModel has 40+ get/set properties including raw string Status, VersionStatus, and PublishStatus fields; the IsShortcut() helper method is the only domain logic present; no invariant enforcement.

invariants: A shortcut's OriginItemId must resolve to an existing item
An item's TypeId must correspond to a registered ContentType
A deleted item cannot be the target of new shortcuts

domains.name: Publish
domains.responsibility: Orchestrates the full content publication pipeline including immediate publish, scheduled publish, simplified publish, promote, and SBP profile-based publishing.
domains.health_reason: Publish eligibility checks (content type publishability, checkout state, permission validation) live inside PublishWriter static methods; PublishTaskEntity does not exist — publish state is tracked as raw strings on ItemModel.PublishStatus.

invariants: Non-publishable content types (e.g. folders) cannot be published
A checked-out file cannot be published unless by the checkout owner
A scheduled publish cannot be set to a past date
A file in an active approval workflow cannot be directly published

domains.name: Permission
domains.responsibility: Controls content access rights, sharing, unique permissions, and granular permission settings for users and groups on content items.
domains.health_reason: IContentPermissionManager and IPermissionCheckerOrchestrator show some interface abstraction, but permission grant/revoke logic is spread across PermissionWriter and PermissionOrchestrator rather than enforced by a PermissionGrantEntity.

invariants: Owner permission cannot be revoked from the last owner
UniquePermission cannot be granted on content that inherits from team-site-level permissions without first breaking inheritance
System identity cannot have its admin permissions modified

domains.name: TeamSite
domains.responsibility: Manages team site (workspace) creation, membership, configuration, and activity tracking within a tenant.
domains.health_reason: TeamSiteEntity exists conceptually in LibraryService.Abstractions.TeamSite but is a plain model; TeamSiteReader/TeamSiteWriter contain the business logic rather than the entity.

invariants: A team site must have at least one admin member
A team site cannot be deleted while it contains active content items
A user cannot be added to a team site if their tenant does not match the team site tenant

domains.name: Search
domains.responsibility: Provides full-text search, AI/ML-powered content recommendations, content queries, and list-view indexing across library content.
domains.health_reason: SearchProducer correctly publishes to Kafka but SearchMessageClient contains business logic (feature toggle checks, topic routing decisions) that belongs in a domain service; query models are plain DTOs without validation.

invariants: A search query must have at least one filter or keyword term
AI/ML queries require caller to have content visibility permission

domains.name: Profile
domains.responsibility: Manages content profiles (content collections mapped to audience segments), custom properties, custom property merge jobs, programs, and activation rules.
domains.health_reason: ContentProfile objects carry raw metadata; CustomProperty domain logic (merge rules, value validation) lives in CustomPropertyMergeStepExecutor background service and PropertyJobExecutor rather than in domain entities.

invariants: A custom property value must conform to its definition's domain of values if constrained
A profile cannot be deleted while it has active content mappings
An activation rule cannot reference a non-existent content profile

domains.name: ExternalSync
domains.responsibility: Synchronizes content from external systems including Google Drive, cloud content repositories, ECM systems, MicroApps, and data sources.
domains.health_reason: IExternalSyncService/IExternalSyncManager/IExternalSyncRepository show a proper layered separation but the ExternalSyncEntity does not enforce sync state invariants — status transitions are managed by the service layer.

invariants: An external sync cannot be re-triggered while already in syncing state
A disconnected external system connection cannot have new content imports initiated
Content imported from external system must retain its ExternalId link

domains.name: Review
domains.responsibility: Manages content review and approval workflow including submitting content for review, recording reviewer decisions, and tracking workflow state.
domains.health_reason: ReviewWriter.AddContentReviews creates ScopedExpressContext via service locator, performs user existence validation, and composes review messages — none of these belong in the infrastructure layer. ReviewEntity does not exist as a domain object.

invariants: A review cannot be submitted for content already in an active review workflow
A reviewer cannot review their own content
A review decision cannot be changed after it has been finalized

domains.name: ContentEngagement
domains.responsibility: Tracks user engagement with content through annotations, inline comments, activities, ask-expert requests, and notifications.
domains.health_reason: AnnotationWriter, ActivityWriter, and CommentWriter are all static classes using service locator; engagement entities are plain data containers with no behavioral methods.

invariants: An annotation cannot be edited by a user other than its author
A resolved annotation cannot accept new reply comments
An expert request must reference a valid user with expert designation

domains.name: ContentDelivery
domains.responsibility: Manages content viewing, rendition generation, LiveDoc/Article/Freestyle dynamic content, content expiration rules, and universal player presentation.
domains.health_reason: ContentView, Rendition, LiveDoc, and Expiration models are plain DTOs; rendering decisions and expiration logic are scattered across ContentViewWriter, ExpirationWriter, and RenditionReader static classes with direct orchestrator calls.

invariants: A rendition cannot be served for an expired content item without explicit override
A LiveDoc content cannot be published without at least one non-empty section
A content view token expires after its configured TTL

domains.name: SystemAdministration
domains.responsibility: Manages system-level configuration, feature toggles, background job administration, cache refresh, dark data tools, and internal API endpoints for operations and integration partners.
domains.health_reason: These are infrastructure/cross-cutting concerns without meaningful domain invariants; the existing service abstractions (IFeatureToggleService, ICacheRemoverService) are appropriately thin.

invariants: A deprecated feature toggle cannot be re-enabled without explicit migration
Cache refresh scope must be bounded to a valid team site or tenant

steps.label: Business validation: batch size limit, already-checked-out guard in Writer
SearchProducer — publish index update to eventbus.public.search.ingest
Content type publishability check in PublishWriter (not in entity)
Checkout ownership validation in PublishWriter (not in entity)
SearchMessageClient — publish to private.search.legacy-action-received or eventbus.public.search.ingest
User existence validation in ReviewWriter (not in aggregate)
ScheduleActivateJobExecutor — queries pending scheduled publish jobs from DB
Content state validation in PublishWriter (not in entity)
FileWriter.CreateFile — creates file entity in CMS

gap_analysis.title: Static Writer/Reader classes use service locator pattern
gap_analysis.detail: FileWriter, PublishWriter, ReviewWriter, FolderWriter and all other Express Writer/Reader classes create ScopedExpressContext via 'new ScopedExpressContext()' and resolve services via ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() / GetScopedService<T>() — completely bypassing the ASP.NET Core DI container. This means these classes cannot be unit-tested, cannot have their dependencies replaced, and create ambient state via a hidden context object rather than explicit parameters.

gap_analysis.title: OrchestratorFactory bypasses DI with direct construction
gap_analysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.CreateFolderOrchestrator(), CreateContentOrchestrator(), etc. construct concrete implementations directly (e.g. 'new SQLFolderOrchestrator(context)') instead of resolving from the DI container. This tightly couples all Writer classes to SQL implementations, prevents interface substitution for testing, and makes it impossible to register cross-cutting concerns (logging, tracing) via DI middleware.

gap_analysis.title: ItemModel is an anemic domain model
gap_analysis.detail: ItemModel contains 40+ public get/set properties including Status (string), VersionStatus (string), PublishStatus (string), ApprovalStatus (string), IsCheckedOut (bool), and IsExpired (bool) — all mutable from outside the class with no invariant enforcement. The only behavioral method is IsShortcut(), a read-only helper. State transitions (checkout, expiry, publish) are performed by Writer classes directly mutating these properties.

gap_analysis.title: Business rules enforced in Writer layer instead of aggregates
gap_analysis.detail: PublishWriter.DeleteSchedulePublish() contains: null check for file existence, file.TeamSiteId cross-team-site ownership check, checkout ownership validation, and content type publishability check. ReviewWriter.AddContentReviews() contains: userId existence validation, user info null check, and review message composition. These are all domain invariants that belong inside aggregate methods.

gap_analysis.title: Status fields modeled as raw strings instead of typed value objects
gap_analysis.detail: ItemModel.Status, ItemModel.VersionStatus, ItemModel.PublishStatus, and ItemModel.ApprovalStatus are all plain string properties. This means invalid status values can be assigned silently (no compile-time safety), status transition rules cannot be encoded in the type, and all callers must rely on magic strings for comparisons. These should be strongly-typed enums or value objects with valid-transition enforcement.

gap_analysis.title: Multiple versioned controllers duplicate domain logic
gap_analysis.detail: FileController exists in V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, and V3.0 namespaces; FileVersionController exists in V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, V3.0; TeamSiteController in V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, V3.0. Each version contains slightly different delegations to the same Writer classes, creating multiple entry points with duplicated cross-cutting logic (e.g. auth attribute setup) and making it unclear which controller owns the domain.

gap_analysis.title: Raw exception classes thrown without DomainExceptionType mapping
gap_analysis.detail: The codebase throws FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, InvalidParameterException, CheckoutException, ActivateActivatedVersionException and 20+ other ad-hoc exception classes directly. There is no unified DomainExceptionType enum to map domain errors to HTTP status codes — the exception-to-HTTP mapping is scattered across catch blocks in controllers and middleware, making consistent error responses fragile.

gap_analysis.title: Express.Tools contains domain logic that belongs in domain layer
gap_analysis.detail: SearchMessageClient in Express.Tools checks a LaunchDarkly feature toggle ('search-publish-index-events-kafka') to decide whether to route to Kafka or Azure Search, and constructs Kafka payloads inline. This routing decision is domain logic (which search index receives this content?) and should live in a domain service, not a shared tools library.

gap_analysis.title: ContentObjectABTableRouter exposes DB table routing at domain model level
gap_analysis.detail: ContentObjectABTableRouter is referenced in both Domain.Abstraction and LibraryService.Abstractions, exposing the A/B database table routing strategy (a persistence infrastructure concern) as a first-class domain model. Domain entities should not know which database table stores them — this couples the domain model to a specific SQL schema optimization.

gap_analysis.title: Domain.Abstraction project mixes interfaces with concrete DTO/model classes
gap_analysis.detail: Seismic.ContentManagerService.Domain.Abstraction contains both interface definitions (e.g. IFileService) and concrete model/DTO classes (e.g. FileModel, FileVersionModel). This means consumers of the abstraction layer must take a dependency on concrete data structures, violating the purpose of an abstraction layer and making it harder to evolve the model independently of the interface contracts.
